segments.caption: Longevity escape velocity, or LEV, is the state in which medicine extends a person’s remaining life expectancy at least as fast as they age.
segments.speech: Longevity escape velocity, or L E V, is the state in which medicine extends a person's remaining life expectancy at least as fast as they age.

segments.caption: Here is what that would take, according to a preliminary evidence review.
segments.speech: Here is what that would take, according to a preliminary evidence review.

segments.caption: As you age, your remaining life expectancy normally shrinks. In the model, a 70-year-old has about 15.6 years left; a year later, about 15.1.
segments.speech: As you age, your remaining life expectancy normally shrinks. In the model, a seventy year old has about fifteen point six years left. A year later, about fifteen point one.

segments.caption: On the report’s main definition, escape velocity means progress is fast enough that this stops: one year older, one year later, with at least as many expected years left.
segments.speech: On the report's main definition, escape velocity means progress is fast enough that this stops. One year older, one year later, you still have at least as many expected years left.

segments.caption: That would not make anyone immortal. It only means the expected end stops getting closer.
segments.speech: That would not make anyone immortal. It only means the expected end stops getting closer.

segments.caption: Death rates climb steeply with age, roughly doubling every eight years. On a log scale, that is close to a straight line.
segments.speech: Death rates climb steeply with age, roughly doubling every eight years. On a log scale, that is close to a straight line.

segments.caption: Shift that line three years to the right and death rates drop by about 23% at every age. That is three age-years of progress.
segments.speech: Shift that line three years to the right, and death rates drop by about twenty-three percent at every age. That is three age years of progress.

segments.caption: On the report’s main definition, escape velocity needs one age-year of progress every calendar year: death rates falling about 8% a year (7–9%), at every age from 50 to 90.
segments.speech: On the report's main definition, escape velocity needs one age year of progress every calendar year. That means death rates falling by about eight percent a year, somewhere between seven and nine, at every age from fifty to ninety.

segments.caption: Compare that with history. Since 1900, overall death rates are reported to have fallen about 1–2% a year.
segments.speech: Compare that with history. Since nineteen hundred, overall death rates are reported to have fallen by about one to two percent a year.

segments.caption: On the report’s main definition, the required pace is four to eight times faster than the observed all-cause pace.
segments.speech: On the report's main definition, the required pace is four to eight times faster than the observed all cause pace.

segments.caption: Other definitions ask for between about 4% and 17% a year, at ages 50 to 80. Whichever you choose, the pace has to rise several-fold.
segments.speech: Other definitions ask for between about four and seventeen percent a year, at ages fifty to eighty. Whichever you choose, the pace has to rise several-fold.

segments.caption: What has medicine actually delivered? The best-demonstrated effects on mortality come from blood pressure, cholesterol, and some diabetes and weight-loss drugs.
segments.speech: What has medicine actually delivered? The best demonstrated effects on mortality come from blood pressure, cholesterol, and some diabetes and weight loss drugs.

segments.caption: Each is a one-off shift worth roughly one to five age-years, mostly in people who already have a disease. A step up, not a new rate.
segments.speech: Each is a one-off shift worth roughly one to five age years, mostly in people who already have a disease. A step up, not a new rate.

segments.caption: To hold one age-year a year, a new step of that size would have to arrive every one to five years, and stack on the last. Nothing shows they do.
segments.speech: To hold one age year a year, a new step of that size would have to arrive every one to five years, and stack on the last. Nothing shows that they do.

segments.caption: Even that is not enough. Mouse-scale steps of 20 age-years every 20 years pass the year-by-year test in only 5% of years, or 22% with smoothing.
segments.speech: Even that is not enough. Mouse scale steps of twenty age years, every twenty years, pass the year by year test in only five percent of years, or twenty-two percent with smoothing.

segments.caption: Lab results look more promising. In mice, the best regimens extend median lifespan by a quarter to a third, though often in one sex or against earlier cohorts.
segments.speech: Lab results look more promising. In mice, the best regimens extend median lifespan by a quarter to a third, though often in one sex, or against earlier cohorts.

segments.caption: If gains like that carried over to people in full, which nothing shows, they would be worth up to about 27 age-years.
segments.speech: If gains like that carried over to people in full, which nothing shows, they would be worth up to about twenty-seven age years.

segments.caption: That is an upper bound, not a finding. No intervention presented as targeting ageing has yet shown a human mortality benefit in the programmes reviewed.
segments.speech: That is an upper bound, not a finding. No intervention presented as targeting aging has yet shown a human mortality benefit in the programs reviewed.

segments.caption: There is a catch. Suppose part of age-related risk resists every treatment.
segments.speech: There is a catch. Suppose part of age related risk resists every treatment.

segments.caption: In the model, if 5% resists and never improves, a no-shrink escape lasts about 12 years. At 10%, about 2. At 20%, none within 60 years.
segments.speech: In the model, if five percent resists and never improves, a no-shrink escape lasts about twelve years. At ten percent, about two. At twenty percent, none within sixty years.

segments.caption: The brain is the obvious candidate for stubborn risk. The report treats it as the hard case: a labelled judgment, not a finding.
segments.speech: The brain is the obvious candidate for stubborn risk. The report treats it as the hard case: a labeled judgment, not a finding.

segments.caption: So when? The evidence cannot separate four outcomes: stagnation, acceleration that falls short of escape, escape starting by 2060, or a later start.
segments.speech: So when? The evidence cannot separate four outcomes: stagnation, acceleration that falls short of escape, escape starting by twenty sixty, or a later start.

segments.caption: The model shows what each date demands. For a start around 2035, the pace must climb from 1.5% a year to about 8% within roughly nine years, then keep at least that pace.
segments.speech: The model shows what each date demands. For a start around twenty thirty-five, the pace must climb from one point five percent a year to about eight percent within roughly nine years, then keep at least that pace.

segments.caption: Nothing in this capped search shows a route to that, so the author judges it unsupported. That is a labelled judgment, not a measurement.
segments.speech: Nothing in this capped search shows a route to that, so the author judges it unsupported. That is a labeled judgment, not a measurement.

segments.caption: Later dates depend on steps not yet seen. Neither “by 2060” nor “not this century” is contradicted, and the report offers no probability.
segments.speech: Later dates depend on steps not yet seen. Neither by twenty sixty, nor not this century, is contradicted, and the report offers no probability.

segments.caption: For one person, it is a race. Suppose escape began thirty years from now.
segments.speech: For one person, it is a race. Suppose escape began thirty years from now.

segments.caption: Someone who is 40 today would have about an 84% chance of being alive for it. At 50, 67%. At 60, 39%. At 70, 11%.
segments.speech: Someone who is forty today would have about an eighty-four percent chance of being alive for it. At fifty, sixty-seven percent. At sixty, thirty-nine percent. At seventy, eleven percent.

segments.caption: These depend on the assumed mortality level, and on an onset the evidence does not show. Age at onset matters a great deal. Separately, the best-supported levers today are ordinary prevention, not a route to escape velocity.
segments.speech: These depend on the assumed mortality level, and on an onset the evidence does not show. Age at onset matters a great deal. Separately, the best supported levers today are ordinary prevention, not a route to escape velocity.

segments.caption: How far should you trust this? Confidence is high in the arithmetic, low to moderate in the evidence, and low on dates. It is a preliminary review built from web-search summaries, not the original papers.
segments.speech: How far should you trust this? Confidence is high in the arithmetic, low to moderate in the evidence, and low on dates. It is a preliminary review built from web search summaries, not from the original papers.

segments.caption: AI agents from a single model family did every step, and no human has checked a figure, a citation or a calculation.
segments.speech: A I agents from a single model family did every step, and no human has checked a figure, a citation or a calculation.

segments.caption: What would change the conclusions: a human mortality result for a treatment that targets ageing itself, and better mortality data by age and decade.
segments.speech: What would change the conclusions: a human mortality result for a treatment that targets aging itself, and better mortality data by age and decade.
